summary: Final weekly POC sync and business-case closeout for the Beacon Retail pilot. Reviewed quantitative results (latency, accuracy, cost), tuning changes made during pilot, open security/procurement items, and agreed next steps toward production decision. Overall outcome: pilot met core success criteria (intent match & throughput) but finance needs final cost comparison for Dedicated vs hosted. Action items assigned for final report, sizing, and procurement follow-up.
topics: Pilot results: latency, accuracy, token cost
Business-case next steps and procurement timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for hopping on. We have about 45 minutes; main goal today is a quick run through of the final pilot metrics, confirm success criteria, and agree next steps for the procurement/exec readout.
[00:14] Laura Chen: Yep, thanks Samir. We'll kick off from product side, but wanted to make sure procurement is on too - Oscar is here.
[00:21] Oscar Rivera: Yep, I'm on. Quick note - procurement will need the final pricing delta between hosted and dedicated, and any SOW or support terms.
[00:30] Jules Kim: Hi everyone, Jules from Redwood SE. I'll run the metrics side and the recommended config if you decide to go Dedicated.
[00:36] Marcus Ng: Marcus here. We ran the pilot on the live catalog subset - ~120k SKUs, traffic shaped to peak hour patterns.
[00:43] Samir Patel: Perfect, Jules, can you start with the headline numbers?
[00:47] Jules Kim: Sure. So over the two-week pilot we ran 48k inference requests through the Redwood hosted endpoint and a short 24-hour Dedicated-style test. Key metrics: p50 latency for the generation route averaged 270 ms on hosted across peak windows, p95 at 780 ms. Token cost averaged $0.00095 per response (normalized). Intent match accuracy measured via the annotated eval set is 94.7% F1. We hit throughput targets of ~120 rps in batching windows with the KV cache enabled.
[01:28] Priya Shah: Quick clarification, Jules - the 94.7% is on the holdout prompts we gave you, right? Not the live production stream?
[01:34] Jules Kim: Correct, that's on the curated eval set you supplied. On live traffic sampled QA checks, intent match looked slightly lower - around 92.9% - we traced a few misses to edge-case prompts with novel product attributes.
[01:47] Laura Chen: So that meets our 92% threshold we set, right? Our success criteria doc had 92% intent match and sub-300 ms p50 during normal load.
[01:55] Samir Patel: Yeah, from the Redwood perspective that's a pass on the two core criteria: p50 and intent threshold. We do flag p95 spikes as an area we'd optimize.
[02:03] Jules Kim: Right - p95 spikes were mostly during cold-cache windows for rare long-history requests. We applied KV prefix caching mid-pilot which dropped p95 spikes by ~18% in subsequent runs.
[02:15] Marcus Ng: The caching approach is fine but we need to be sure it won't mis-handle personalized context for returns and exchanges. Did you see any regressions on the personalized intents?
[02:24] Jules Kim: Good call. We instrumented guard rails - cache keyed on conversation prefix and user session id. We didn't see personalization regressions in the sample; Priya can attest from the analytics.
[02:34] Priya Shah: Yep, we ran the regression suite - no statistically significant drop on personalization-based intents. There were a handful of false positives around synonyms and SKU abbreviations. We added a lightweight normalization step in the request pipeline during week two which helped.
[02:49] Samir Patel: Great. Oscar, from procurement standpoint, how are you thinking about timelines?
[02:54] Oscar Rivera: We'll need final numbers to compare Dedicated commit vs pay-as-you-go hosted. Also need SOC 2 and encryption/KMS details. If the numbers look reasonable, legal and finance want to move in the next two weeks.
[03:06] Samir Patel: Understood. We'll include SOC 2 scope, SSO/SAML notes, and KMS integration options in the packet.
[03:12] Laura Chen: Any surprises on data residency? We had that as a requirement for EU orders.
[03:17] Jules Kim: For the pilot data residency was using the US region. For production, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem deployments; Dedicated can be provisioned in EU region - we can include region-specific SLA language.
[03:30] Marcus Ng: On cost - can you spell out the runtime delta if we go Dedicated with the suggested q4 quantization versus staying hosted with continuous batching?
[03:39] Jules Kim: Sure. Short answer: Dedicated amortizes per-token cost if your baseline throughput remains high; our recommended Dedicated config (2 x A100-equivalent pools, mixed-precision quantization) reduces per-token cost by ~30% compared to current hosted usage. But there's an upfront reserved capacity commitment - for Beacon's traffic profile that payback is roughly 6-8 months in our model. We'll give the detailed spreadsheet.
[04:02] Laura Chen: OK that's reasonable. Finance will want the 6-8 month calc and sensitivity to traffic dips.
[04:09] Samir Patel: We'll include a sensitivity tab showing traffic -20% and +30%.
[04:14] Priya Shah: On the technical side, Jules, you mentioned a Dedicated short test - did you change model variants between hosted and Dedicated?
[04:21] Jules Kim: We used the same base model family but switched to a 4-bit quantized variant on Dedicated test. We also bumped batch sizes to exploit the GPU memory headroom, and that’s where the cost reduction came from. Accuracy delta from quantization was <0.6% absolute on our eval suite.
[04:40] Marcus Ng: That delta is acceptable. Any concerns about cold-starts or autoscaling during seasonal spikes?
[04:46] Jules Kim: For Dedicated we recommend a small warm standby pool and autoscale policy to absorb spikes; Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and graceful fallback to hosted model family if you hit committed capacity limits. So resiliency is covered.
[05:00] Laura Chen: What about observability - token-level cost breakouts and per-route latency dashboards? We need that for product dashboards.
[05:07] Samir Patel: Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics, token breakdowns, and trace hooks. We'll share sample dashboards and can set up a short walkthrough for your product analytics team.
[05:18] Oscar Rivera: Also include retention and audit log retention windows - our security team will ask.
[05:23] Jules Kim: We'll include default retention and options for extended retention as an add-on.
[05:28] Samir Patel: Okay let's pivot to the business-case alignment. Laura, does product still feel comfortable recommending go/no-go based on the current results?
[05:35] Laura Chen: I think product is comfortable provisionally, but we need finance's buy-in. The product KPIs are met. The remaining blockers are procurement and legal on terms.
[05:45] Oscar Rivera: For legal we'll need a redlineable master services agreement and the SOC 2 report. If we get those and the numbers check out, procurement can finalize in roughly a week.
[05:55] Samir Patel: Good. Jules, any technical risks you'd call out for the board readout?
[06:01] Jules Kim: Risk list: (1) edge-case prompt drift - we'll recommend an ongoing eval harness; (2) cold-cache p95 spikes - mitigations are warm pools and pre-warming strategies; (3) vendor lock-in concerns - we'll propose a model-version pinning policy and fallback routes.
[06:20] Marcus Ng: On the eval harness, can Redwood run periodic backtests against new catalog changes automatically?
[06:26] Jules Kim: Yes - we can integrate an eval pipeline that runs on deploy and flags regressions against your baseline prompts.
[06:30] Priya Shah: We want automated alerts if F1 drops >2% across critical intents. Can you support that?
[06:36] Jules Kim: Yep, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring and regression alerts; we'll include rule examples.
[06:40] Samir Patel: All right, quick recap of agreed deliverables: Samir sends final packet + metrics by Friday; Jules sends Dedicated sizing and quant spreadsheet; Laura to confirm success criteria doc; Oscar to kick off procurement.
[06:55] Laura Chen: I'll confirm and share the updated success criteria by Tuesday.
[07:00] Oscar Rivera: Procurement will start internal review once we have the packet; expecting questions on indemnity and data processing addendum.
[07:08] Samir Patel: We'll surface DPA and standard liability language. Jules, anything else on the tech side?
[07:13] Jules Kim: I'll add notes about quantization, cache keying, and the small warm pool recommendation. Also include monitoring dashboards.
[07:20] Marcus Ng: One last operational note - we need an emergency rollback plan if a model rollout causes regressions. Do you have runbooks?
[07:26] Jules Kim: Yes, policies include canary rollouts, automatic fallback to previous pinned model, and immediate alerting. We'll attach the runbook excerpt.
[07:36] Samir Patel: Excellent. Any other questions?
[07:39] Priya Shah: None from data science.
[07:41] Laura Chen: No.
[07:42] Oscar Rivera: Not right now.
[07:44] Samir Patel: Great - we'll share the documents and follow up. Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[07:50] <<meeting end>>
